name: Coinbase

summary.text: Coinbase is a U.S. cryptocurrency exchange led by chief executive Brian Armstrong. FactCheck.org identifies it as one of the three largest contributors to the crypto super PAC Fairshake, alongside Ripple Labs and Andreessen Horowitz. It gave Fairshake $25 million in June 2024 and in October 2024 announced a further $25 million for the 2026 midterms. Armstrong has said the company's aim is to elect pro-crypto candidates of both parties and vote anti-crypto candidates out of office.

facts.claim: In early June 2024 Coinbase gave $25 million to the Fairshake super PAC, days after President Biden vetoed a congressional resolution on crypto custody accounting; Ripple and Andreessen Horowitz had each given $25 million in late May 2024.

facts.claim: Brian Armstrong wrote in 2024 that 'The best way to get regulatory clarity in democratic countries is to elect pro-crypto candidates on both sides of the aisle, and to vote anti-crypto candidates out of office,' in explaining Coinbase's $25 million support for Fairshake.

facts.claim: On October 30, 2024 Armstrong announced on X that Coinbase would give Fairshake a further $25 million in 2025 for the 2026 midterms, saying the next Congress 'will be the most pro-crypto' yet and 'we're not slowing down'. On November 4, 2024 Fairshake said it had raised $78 million for 2026 including new commitments from Coinbase and Andreessen Horowitz.

facts.claim: FactCheck.org identifies Coinbase, Ripple Labs and AH Capital Management (Andreessen Horowitz) as Fairshake's largest contributors. Wikipedia, citing FEC data, puts Coinbase's giving to Fairshake since 2023 at $93.5 million; this figure should be checked against FEC filings.
The Washington Post reported that the Fairshake-network ads it viewed in the 2024 cycle did not mention crypto and that the super PACs were backed by Coinbase and Ripple.

openQuestions: Not recorded (search budget exhausted before sec.gov results were obtained): the SEC's June 2023 suit against Coinbase and its February 2025 dismissal. No 'sec' connection is recorded for that reason.
Basic company facts (founding year, Nasdaq listing in 2021) were not sourced in this run.

Coinbase's total giving to Fairshake differs by source and period: more than $75 million (NBC/CNBC, 2024 cycle, in fairshake.json), about $93.5 million (Bloomberg Government analysis of FEC data as cited by Wikipedia, 2023-2024), and $52.46 million for the 2026 cycle (Wikipedia). Fortune reported Coinbase had also given more than $20 million in 2023. None of these was verified at the FEC.
The Armstrong 'regulatory clarity' quote was attributed in search results to a 2024 blog post; the Fox Business article is cited as the carrier. The owner should confirm the original post.
Reports that Armstrong personally gave $1 million to Fairshake and that a 2025 gift was $24.5 million from Coinbase plus $1 million from Armstrong came from aggregator sites and are not recorded.
